attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. The quoted Planet Money passage nearby is separate from the claim.

semantics.note: The claim keeps both parts: customers resisting prices is the cause, and efficiency is ruled out. 'These price cuts' were cuts under consideration in June, not cuts already made.

contract.note: Tying the claim to the June deliberations and requiring evidence for both the cause and the excluded cause is a fair reading. Pinning down which cuts he meant is the contract's inference, not his.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous June 11 report. It tentatively links the move to users balking at costs and to competition, but does not establish motives or rule out efficiency.
OpenAI's own July 30 disclosure credits efficiency for a later cut. It is a company statement about a different decision, so context only.
Anthropic's own September 22 disclosure links Opus 5.5 pricing to lower serving compute. It concerns a later decision, not the June deliberations.

reviews.rationale: The only contemporaneous source is consistent with customer cost resistance but is tentative, and it does not rule out efficiency as a cause. The company efficiency explanations cover later, different cuts and are self-disclosures. No source in the packet settles what drove the June deliberations.

attribution.note: Zitron endorses SemiAnalysis's model in his own words ('That's right folks'). The claim is his statement of what that model shows.

semantics.note: The claim keeps the 75% token-margin assumption, the 25% utilization level and the 'at best' bound. It is a claim about the model's arithmetic, not actual company margins.

contract.note: Testing the stated model's arithmetic across the cited tiers matches what he said. The contract correctly bars actual margins from replacing the assumption.

evidence.note: Dated June 10 reproduction of SemiAnalysis's inputs. Applying the 25% cost ratio at 25% utilization gives -25% for the two lower Claude tiers and worse margins for every other tier. The breakeven figures it reports agree.

reviews.rationale: Under the stated 75% margin assumption, the reproduced tier inputs give a best-case margin of exactly -25% at 25% utilization (Claude Pro and Max 5x), with all other tiers worse. The arithmetic checks out. The numbers come from a secondary reproduction, not the original tables.

attribution.note: His own comment on the WSJ passage he quotes. The quoted executives and Citadel are not part of the claim.

semantics.note: The claim keeps both parts: no proof that running these models is profitable or sustainable for any provider, and no tangible proof they compete at scale with OpenAI or Anthropic models.

contract.note: The readings of 'proof', 'profitable' and 'at scale' are reasonable but not supplied by him. Requiring a broad review to show something is absent is fair.

evidence.note: DeepSeek's margin figure assumes all usage is billed at R1 prices, and the document says actual revenue is lower. Not proof of realized profit, but one company's disclosure does not show proof is absent everywhere.
Fireworks's own claim of large-scale production adoption. Vendor marketing with no matched frontier comparison and no profit accounts, so it falls short of the contract's bar.
A 2024 study comparing small open models with a GPT-4 product feature. Its comparator is old and its scope narrow, so it does not show competing at scale with mid-2026 models.

reviews.rationale: Neither part is settled. No realized hosting-profit record appears, but a limited search cannot prove there is none. The adoption and comparison evidence is vendor-sourced or old and narrow, so it neither meets the contradiction bar nor shows the absence the support condition requires.

attribution.note: His own words. The WSJ and Cisco quotes nearby belong to others.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'would be deadly' conditional on the contemplated cuts. The wording is hyperbolic, and his follow-up describes margins being 'eaten alive', which is milder than industry collapse.

contract.note: Reading 'deadly' as lasting loss of financial viability is plausible but supplied by the contract. Marking the condition 'met' is doubtful, because the September cuts on new models may not be the June proposals.

evidence.note: Shows both companies cut token prices on new models on September 22. This bears on the condition, not the predicted outcome, and may not match the June cuts.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated and no conclusive event is documented: the packet shows no industry failure attributable to the cuts and no proof of durable viability. Whether the condition was met is also uncertain. Under the rules, an undated forecast without a conclusive event stays unresolved.
